title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two Rio Arriba County sisters sued Española over a July 23 traffic stop. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, and her 12 year old sister were pulled over on Calle Duran after a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate as belonging to a stolen vehicle from Rio Rancho. The plate differed by one digit, ending in 2 instead of 7, according to the lawsuits. Officers handcuffed them and placed them in police vehicles before learning of the error. Jaclynn asked an officer to call their mother for the younger sister, but the girl was handcuffed and placed in a different police vehicle, the complaints say.

The sisters filed separate lawsuits Jan. 3 in state District Court. They seek unspecified damages and compensation for personal injuries, including distress and restricted movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, filed a similar complaint in April for Adam Pacheco, then 17, who was mistakenly stopped as an armed robbery suspect and forced to kneel in the road. Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment.
